title_candidates: AI agents tried to reproduce 2,200 ICML papers
summary: A public ICML project used coding agents to test claims from 2,226 papers, revealing both useful checks and serious agent-made errors.

primary_source.title: What We Learned by Reproducing 2,200 papers from ICML
primary_source.author: Hugging Face
key_facts: The challenge involved 1,221 community members, 6,816 public logbooks, and 2,226 attempted ICML papers.
The attempts covered 35,908 claims across about 34% of the conference.
At least one claim was independently verified in 51% of examined papers, while 23% had at least one falsified or contested claim.
Organizers treated automated verdicts and logbook self-assessments as untrusted.
Manual rechecks found both genuine paper problems and serious errors in attempted reproductions.
The strongest results combined agent execution with active human oversight.

supporting_sources.title: ICML 2026 Open Reproductions gallery
key_facts: The public gallery links paper-level reproduction logbooks, artifacts, and verdicts.

supporting_sources.title: Reproducing ICML 2026 challenge
key_facts: The public challenge Space provides access to project records and instructions.

prerequisites: No research or coding account required

steps.instruction: Choose one paper in the public gallery and inspect the exact claim, evidence, scale, missing inputs, and any independent attempts.
Separate the original claim from the reproduction's result and treat automated verdicts without human rechecking as provisional.

references.title: What We Learned by Reproducing 2,200 papers from ICML
references.author: Hugging Face

risk_flags: Challenge verdict percentages describe attempted reproductions and must not be generalized to all ICML papers.
A falsified or verified badge is not conclusive without inspecting the experiment, scale, artifacts, and human recheck.
